liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **China Cat Sunflower** (4 reviews): The reviewer lists this performance as one of their personal favorites; The band extended the jam, delaying the verse for several minutes before singing [10][12][14][20]
- **Eyes Of The World** (3 reviews): The performance of this song is cited as one of the best in the world; The encore performance is noted as being very strong [10][13][19]
- **The Other One** (2 reviews): The transition into the Spanish Jam exemplifies why 1974 is a favorite year; The jam following this song is highlighted as defining the reviewer's fandom [13][20]
- **Truckin'** (1 review): The performance of this song is described as snappy [12]

## The recordings

- **gd74-06-26.moore.weiner.gdADT17.16037.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): audience recording; 29 songs; 237 min; rated 4.5/5 by 30 [1]. Said about its sound: The audience recording is superb, though the Eyes encore audio clips at the end; The recording allows listeners to feel as if they are back in the venue [16][17]
- **gd1974-06-26.149947.mtx.seamons.ht119.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 27 songs; 234 min; rated 5/5 by 3 [3]. Said about its sound: A blown speaker during Scarlet Begonias caused metallic vocal reverb in Black Throated Wind; Vocal quality improved during Row Jimmy and subsequent songs in the second set; U.S. Blues had bad initial soundboard mix, so the audience tape is used until the chorus [3]
- **gd74-06-26.sbd.oleynick.214.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 28 songs; 184 min; rated 4.5/5 by 10 [2]
- **gd1974-06-26.akgd1000e.moore.berger.105919.flac24**: audience recording; 27 songs; 238 min; rated 4.67/5 by 6 [4]

## Around the show

- The band released the album Mars Hotel the day after this show [14]
- The recording includes hilarious comments from the audience, referred to as the peanut gallery [16]
- The venue is affectionately called Quahog Heaven, located in Providence, Rhode Island [19]
- The reviewer attended the concert on their seventeenth birthday [21]
- This show is considered slightly stronger than the June 28, 1974 performance [13]
- Listeners are advised to choose the May 17, 1974 show if selecting based on this [15]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd74-06-26.moore.weiner.gdADT17.16037.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Jerry Moore; source: Audience Recording: Sony ECM-99 Stereo mic [1]. Also: Jerry Moore recorded the audience tape near the rear center using Sony ECM-99 mics; The audio lineage includes AudMC, WAV, CD, EAC, and SHN formats [1]
- **gd1974-06-26.149947.mtx.seamons.ht119.flac16**: transferred by Matrix by Hunter Seamons; source: Matrix by Hunter Seamons using Final Cut Pro (FLAC > AIFF > Final Cut > Soundtrack Pro > AIFF CD tracking via Audacity > FLAC16 via xACT w/meta-tagging) [3]
- **gd74-06-26.sbd.oleynick.214.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [2]
- **gd1974-06-26.akgd1000e.moore.berger.105919.flac24**: taped by Jerry Moore; transferred by Rob Berger; source: aud>akg d1000e's>sony tc-152sd, (3)maxell ud-120's, dolby b [4]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Providence Civic Center - June 26, 1974](https://www.dead.net/show/june-26-1974) [23]
- Fan art by www.rirocks.net: [Grateful Dead 1974 06.26](https://www.rirocks.net/Band%20Articles/Grateful%20Dead%201974%2006.26%20-%20Prov.%20Civic%20Center.htm) [24]
